transcript.text: My Dyson V10 Absolute (SV12) won't run at all now. On the battery display there's a red light flashing when I press the trigger, then nothing. It was charging overnight. Do I need a new battery or is the whole thing dead?
Let’s start by looking at what the battery is doing. On a full charge, does it run only a short time before stopping, or will it not charge at all?

It used to run only a short time, getting worse for months, down to about 8 minutes on the lowest mode. Three days ago it stopped running completely. It does charge, the blue lights come on on the charger, but the motor won't start.

Thanks for letting us know about your Dyson vacuum running out quickly. Please check that the charger is plugged into a working socket and pushed fully into the vacuum or dock. Wipe the charging contacts so they are clean and dry; the charging light should then come on. Was the charger, socket or contacts the problem (and is it sorted), does the charging light never come on, or is the charger fine with the light on?

The charger is fine, the light is on and I tried a different socket (hallway) with the same result. The contacts look clean too. So it's charging but the motor still won't start, just the flashing red on the trigger. Safety-wise, the battery isn't swollen, hot or smelly.

Thanks for letting me know about the RED code and that the unit remains unresponsive despite power being present. I have noted the display reading; this next step is the right place to start regardless of the cause. If the vacuum stopped while you were using it, it may have overheated due to a blockage. Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Leave it to cool for an hour, then check the hose, wand, floorhead and filters for any obstructions. Did you find a blockage and clear it, is there one you can't shift, or was it all clear?

Filter was washed last month, bin is empty and I can't see any blockages in the hose or wand. It didn't stop mid-use though, it just wouldn't start the next time I pressed the trigger. I'm not taking anything apart, in case Dyson need to look at it.

[Heading: Switch, cable or motor inside]
Thank you for the update. Based on what you’ve described, the issue likely lies with the switch, an internal connection, the battery, or the motor, though I cannot confirm which from our current information. This requires assessment by a repairer. Please do not open the unit or test any components inside. I am not recommending any specific part at this stage.
